To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) innovation studies, entrepreneurship studies and science and technology policy studies are three related but separate and distinct fields of research, (b) each of the fields has developed a distinct and coherent knowledge base over the last 30 years, (c) the three fields have developed in different ways and at different rates, and (d) each of the three knowledge bases has developed a number of core contributions that have become widely recognized and influential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the knowledge base of the knowledge society.
the emergence, development and evolution of three research fields that are concerned with the knowledge society.
the development of the three fields, with their relationships, and with the policy challenges that arise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knowledge society is a society in which knowledge, and the production, dissemination and application of knowledge, are of increasing importance.
the three fields are not only distinct but also have different histories, and that the differences are more than a reflection of different academic disciplines.
the ‘knowledge society’ has become a key concept in the social sciences and humanities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the knowledge society is a reality that is increasingly important in our lives.
the knowledge society is a reality but that we still do not have a clear understanding of its implications for policy and governance.
the three fields of entrepreneurship, innovation and science and technology policy have become more interrelated over the last 20 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the knowledge society is not a static concept but rather a dynamic process of knowledge creation and knowledge diffusion.
there are important differences between the three research fields, and that there is a need for more research that explores the relationships between them.
the three fields have grown in size and importance and have developed in different ways, and that they are now at a critical stage in their evolution.
